finding: **Cancelled/partial database-wide enrichment is presented as green completion at 100%.** Per-report exceptions become failed counts/warnings, skips are counted, and cooperative cancellation breaks the loop. The UI nevertheless renders `Metadata enrichment complete: X/Y reports updated`, forces 100% and sets success whenever a result exists and no fatal error signal was recorded. It does not inspect failed/skipped/cancelled/incomplete status.
evidence: `src/metroliza/ui/main_window.py:854–859, 878–912`; `src/metroliza/parsing/metadata_enrichment_thread.py:219–266, 284–285, 341–355`; `src/metroliza/parsing/parse_reports_thread.py:123–140`. The standalone batch also leaves cancellation accounting fields at defaults. No enrichment terminal screenshot exists.
impact: After Cancel, missing sources or individual OCR failures, an expert can trust a green completion and export incompletely enriched metadata. Example derived from the branch: stopping after 20/100 can still produce green “20/100 reports updated” and a full bar.
recommendation: Reuse the import enrichment outcome categories; account explicitly for not-processed cancellation, failures and skips. Show Cancelled or Completed with warnings when appropriate, saved updates retained, and a route to the affected reports. Reserve success for a fully accounted successful/no-work result.

finding: **An existing destination is silently reused, including after changing database.** Re-export retains the path; database change clears filters/groups but not `excel_file`. Export does not repeat a collision decision, and the backend atomically replaces the target. Example: export database A to `A.xlsx`, choose database B, then Export still targets `A.xlsx`. The risk is an unnoticed replacement, not corruption from partial writing.
evidence: `ui/export_dialog.py:1156–1175` retains output; `:1289–1313` collision avoidance runs only while choosing a path; `:1325–1399` starts without an existing-file check; `exporting/contracts.py:117–143` validates strings/extensions; `exporting/export_backends.py:725–727,748–784` replaces target. `shots/07011_ExportDialog__done__light.png` shows the retained path and enabled Export, but the database-switch/replacement sequence was not captured.
impact: A routine next-batch export can destroy the prior deliverable or save a new batch under the old batch's name; recreating/validating the lost workbook can cost minutes.
recommendation: Keep fast re-export, but visibly distinguish **Create** from **Replace existing file**. Rebind/propose the output name when the database changes and require explicit retention of an old destination. Make Save as/new copy accessible beside the output. Preserve atomic publication.

finding: Changing a reference clears Header and Selected headers unconditionally. Even searching Reference after selecting headers calls a helper that clears/reselects the reference selection, invoking the same destructive refresh. Apply then has no header predicate unless the expert reselects it.
evidence: `filter_dialog.py:493–508`, `1006–1029`, `1097–1099`; `src/metroliza/shared/list_selection_utils.py:118–140`. `10002_FilterDialog__populated__light.png` locates the controls; it does not show this transition.
impact: A routine scope revision/search can silently widen a core export from a few headers to all available headers; reselecting many headers adds repeated work.
recommendation: Preserve header selections across reference refresh; retain unavailable selected values with an explicit warning. Make search visibility changes signal-safe so they do not masquerade as predicate edits. Show a visible change notice if a restriction must change.

finding: Invalid nonblank numeric text can be confirmed as typed but persisted as NULL. UI conversion returns unparseable text unchanged; repository conversion silently turns it into None. For example, `10,25` or `abc` in MEAS can clear the value while the normal success path reports completion. This differs from deliberately clearing a cell.
evidence: `U/modify_db_records.py:179–198`; `U/modify_db.py:1046–1057,1172–1177,1198–1207`; `R/report_repository.py:264–272,1327–1343,1437–1446`. Exact-function in-memory probe: `10.25 → 10.25 → 10.25`; `10,25 → '10,25' → None`; `abc → 'abc' → None`. `S/16005_ModifyDB__populated_tab1_3_Measurement_rows__light.png` supplies context only.
impact: Risks losing measured values/tolerances during routine correction and trusting an export with missing values.
recommendation: Validate numeric edits before review; reject nonblank invalid values, show cell-level reason, and retain old data. Define decimal-separator policy explicitly; preview exactly the value that will be persisted.

finding: One confirmed batch is not one atomic save for current-schema databases. Normalization commits first; targeted report/measurement updates follow as separate transactions. A later invalid STATUS_CODE, for example, can fail after normalization/earlier records have committed. The generic error does not identify which subset saved, and the grid still holds the pending overlay.
evidence: `R/report_edit_service.py:69–104,211–244`; `R/report_repository.py:304–308,1327–1343,1460–1476`; `U/modify_db.py:1070–1099,1303–1304`; `src/metroliza/shared/custom_logger.py:45–61,70–82`. Manual recovery already advises closing/reopening after failure: `M/modify_database.md` → “Saving changes fails”.
impact: A failed save leaves the user uncertain what the database/export now contains; retry or Cancel cannot reliably restore the pre-save state.
recommendation: Prevalidate all changes, commit the full confirmed batch in one transaction, and report “Nothing saved” on rollback. Until atomicity exists, expose an exact partial-save result and require reload before further editing.

finding: **Typed search can be ignored by Assign all filtered rows.** All three grouping searches apply only on Enter. The assignment reads `_applied_selector_filter_text`, not the visible text, and there is no textChanged pending marker or click-time synchronization. Type `PART=A` and click Assign all without Enter: the previously applied scope, potentially all rows, is used. The name prompt shows no affected-row count or applied predicate.
evidence: `TG:518–525`, `892–919`, `1801–1824`, `1937–1978`, `2004–2009`, `1017–1031`. S-GP JSON `w29` has no Enter hint/tooltip; `w42` is enabled with blank scope. Contrast database `DG:527–536` and S-DBG's explicit `(Enter)` scope placeholder; live ordinary searches `DG:759–764`, `FD:492–505`. SQLite filter search already supplies a pending message at `TF:656–660`.
impact: Rows outside the intended cohort can be reassigned while the visible search suggests a narrower target. This is more serious than an extra Enter because group assignments affect all analytic outputs.
recommendation: Keep expensive searches Enter-applied if necessary, but show `Not applied — press Enter`, the last applied predicate and matching-row count. Disable assignment while pending, or apply/validate the visible input before assignment. Destination prompt should state target count and any reassignment impact.

finding: First close requests enrichment cancellation and is ignored; when enrichment stops, the shell clears its thread and updates status but never retries close. This differs from Reports/filter/child deferred shutdown.
evidence: No closing-state PNG. `main_window.py:916–919,996–1004,854–860,874–876`; compare automatic retries at `1029–1036,1092–1105`.
impact: The user closes the app, waits for safe cancellation, then finds it still open and must infer that a second close is required.
recommendation: Track the pending close request, show “Stopping metadata enrichment; Metroliza will close when safe,” and retry only after the worker has actually finished. Allow an explicit decision to keep the app open if needed.

finding: A running enrichment task is bound to its original database, but the global row does not name that database and accepted database changes are not blocked by shell enrichment. After switching from A to B, the task/result can appear to describe B.
evidence: No target-switch/enrichment PNG. `main_window.py:854–866,906–912,1600–1615,1683–1706`; `parsing_dialog.py:677–682`; worker stores its own database at `src/metroliza/parsing/metadata_enrichment_thread.py:277–282`; worker status text at `287–304`.
impact: Requires mental tracking of an invisible old target and makes progress/results less trustworthy when preparing another database.
recommendation: Add a persistent task target, e.g. “Enrich metadata · A.sqlite,” with a copyable full path and “Previous database” when it differs from the workspace. Keep task identity through terminal status.

finding: “Export ... remain on their previously selected database. Finish or close them...” remains visible after that old Export closes. The coordinated-window closed handler clears references but does not recompute this notice.
evidence: No A→B/close PNG. `main_window.py:1634–1641,1653–1668,1086–1105`. The warning is cleared on a later database selection at `1613`, not when its cause disappears.
impact: Following the instruction does not resolve the displayed warning; the user cannot tell whether the new context is ready.
recommendation: Derive the notice from live blockers and refresh on open/close/context transitions. Clear only the resolved notice, preserving any other active warning. Add a “Show Export” action while that blocker exists.

window: MainWindow domain landing pages and Tools menu
finding: Priority CSV entry requires a launcher-only intermediate page. Tools “CSV Summary...” navigates to “CSV Analytics,” whose button then opens CSV Summary. Three other domain menu actions similarly navigate rather than open their named workflows.
evidence: `01002_MainMenu_Tools__initial_menu_1__light.png`; landing content/handlers are code-only: `main_window.py:442–458,581–595,693–714,1211–1219`; manual explicitly describes the extra step at `docs/user_manual/main_window.md:25–28,52–54`.
impact: Two clicks from sidebar or three through Tools for a repeated CSV task; inconsistent names create a moment of destination checking.
recommendation: Use one product name, preferably the established “CSV Summary,” and make the Tools action open/raise that workflow directly. Keep sidebar landing pages if useful, but give them real context/status or direct keyboard launch. Preserve Reports state and per-type reuse for coordinated tools.

finding: Shell-owned downstream actions precede the source controls in the composed focus chain, despite appearing below the planner. Focus goes from sidebar to Modify Database, Match Characteristic Names and Export before returning to the top input region.
evidence: `04007_ImportWorkspace__review_planner__light.png` + JSON focusChain: `w2→w6→w7→w8→w18→w29→w30`; bottom buttons at y=704, source field at y=46. Construction order: `main_window.py:575–579,667–682`; shell does not register a composed tab order.
impact: Keyboard users traverse unrelated bottom actions before choosing source/database, then jump back up; the same daily route is harder to predict from the layout.
recommendation: Define tab order after embedding Reports: navigation → source/database → review controls/table → import → downstream actions. Preserve each area's internal order and recheck after conditional controls appear.

finding: **Choosing an existing database can silently select a different filename.** The picker allows All Files, then appends `.db` to every result not ending in lowercase `.db`. Selecting existing `quality.sqlite` yields `quality.sqlite.db`; `quality.DB` yields `quality.DB.db`. If that appended path is absent, review/import address a new database rather than the chosen existing one.
evidence: `src/metroliza/ui/parsing_dialog.py:844–860`; `docs/user_manual/parsing.md:14–15` promises existing/new DB selection and documents suffix addition. `04003_FileDialogSubstitute__initial_file_dialog__light.png`/JSON `w23` shows `.sqlite` input and `w28` All Files, but this is a synthetic substitute, not a runtime reproduction of redirection.
impact: Duplicate recognition runs against the wrong destination; the day's import/export can omit the established database history. The displayed redirected path does not make an unintended destination choice safe. Lowercase `.db` files are unaffected.
recommendation: Preserve the exact path for every selected existing file. Append a default extension only for a genuinely new extensionless name. Distinguish Open existing database from Create new database, with the destination basename and existing/new status visible before review.

finding: **Bulk copy overwrites existing corrections across every checked editable report, including filtered-out rows, with no batch undo.** The menu label omits the field, value and affected/hidden count. Reset to detected operates on one row and discards its manual edits; it cannot recover the previous set of distinct manual values. The issue is insufficient scope/recovery, not global selection itself.
evidence: `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner.py:201–215, 379–403, 430–448`; `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner_model.py:310–313, 353–372`; `src/metroliza/reports/report_metadata_review.py:502–527, 573–585`. The import consumes these overrides at `src/metroliza/ui/parsing_dialog.py:1285–1289`. No bulk-action capture exists.
impact: A reference, sample number or date from one report can replace correct values in an entire checked batch and then be imported. Recovering prior manual values requires re-entry rather than undo.
recommendation: Keep fast bulk editing, but expose “Copy Reference = … to N checked reports (H hidden)”, count existing manual values to replace, and provide one-step batch Undo restoring exact prior values. Add confirmation only when overwriting existing corrections or a materially risky scope, rather than to every routine edit.

finding: **Every terminal import erases the review and metadata draft, leaving only aggregate results.** After a subset import or cancellation, corrections on unimported reports disappear too. The result does not identify which report failed/changed/cancelled, so refreshing is a fresh selection/reconstruction exercise.
evidence: `04009_ImportWorkspace__done__light.png`/JSON `w23` (0 rows), `w29` (saved count/destination); `06009_ImportWorkspace__done__scale150.png`; `src/metroliza/ui/parsing_dialog.py:175–257, 760–779, 1460–1487`; `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner_model.py:469–489`; aggregate-only `ParseBatchResult` at `src/metroliza/parsing/parse_reports_thread.py:73–88`. Normal clearing is captured; partial/cancel branches are source-only.
impact: An expert correcting a mixed batch must rebuild unimported corrections and locate problems after the operation. Counts establish how much happened, but not what to repair or retry.
recommendation: Keep the completed review as a read-only result snapshot with per-report terminal statuses. Disable further import until a fresh review. Carry a separate metadata draft for unchanged unimported identities through revalidation; do not carry stale approval. Offer Review remaining/retry candidates and expose failed/changed file identities with safe reasons.

finding: **A metadata-policy or context change silently discards inline corrections.** `currentIndexChanged` immediately invalidates the review with no dirty-draft guard. The generic invalidated status appears only after the rows and corrections are gone. The manual documents invalidation but does not explain loss of inline edits.
evidence: `src/metroliza/ui/parsing_dialog.py:484–486, 663–675, 760–784`; `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner_model.py:469–489`; `docs/user_manual/parsing.md:63–66`. Refresh already has fingerprint/parser-bound carry support at `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner_model.py:395–425`. No edited-state capture exists.
impact: An expert who fixes headers and then chooses OCR/enrichment can lose several minutes of corrections. Undoing the combo selection does not restore them.
recommendation: Preserve a separate dirty metadata draft for unchanged identities across the mandatory re-review. If it cannot be preserved, warn only when a change would discard edits, show the edited-report count and offer Keep current context. Make “not saved until Import” visible near editing.

finding: **Readiness is visually stronger than metadata quality.** The captured batch shows a green “Review complete…all have a reference” and twelve “Ready to import” statuses while all twelve reports need attention. Amber italic values have no visible legend. The reason is in cell tooltips/details or a far-right column; assistive metadata text gives value but not low-confidence/conflict state.
evidence: `04007_ImportWorkspace__review_planner__light.png`/JSON `w21`, `w37`; `05007_ImportWorkspace__review_planner__dark.png`; `src/metroliza/ui/parsing_dialog.py:628, 650–661`; `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner_metadata.py:101–120, 142–153, 156–190, 288–296`; `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner_model.py:677–715, 774–780`.
impact: Experts must reconcile “ready” with “need attention” and inspect values individually to learn whether they are filename guesses, missing values or OCR conflicts. Parser eligibility can be mistaken for metadata verification.
recommendation: Retain nonblocking import eligibility, but state “12 importable · 12 metadata warnings” with a direct attention filter. Add concise textual field/row warning indicators and a compact legend; include state and provenance in accessible descriptions. Do not require clearing every optional metadata warning to import.

finding: **OCR can fill fields that remain hidden, and neither the UI nor parsing manual explains how to expose/edit them.** Time, Revision, Operator and Comment start hidden. Columns are enabled only through a custom header context menu; no visible Columns command or explicit keyboard equivalent is wired. Editing hints are in tooltips, while the manual omits inline editing, Read with OCR, Copy/Reset and that header menu.
evidence: `04007`/`05007`/`06007` review-planner PNGs/JSON headers; `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner.py:95, 163–167, 417–428, 545–554`; `src/metroliza/reports/report_metadata_review.py:36–62`; `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner_model.py:584–590`; `docs/user_manual/parsing.md:30–44, 68–71` and remainder of the 76-line manual. OCR completion visibility is source-based, not captured.
impact: An expert can run OCR without discovering the newly filled header fields, or miss pre-import correction entirely. Inspecting a long technical details pane is a costly substitute for editable columns.
recommendation: Add a compact keyboard-reachable Columns menu with a Metadata fields group and a view preset for OCR fields. Expose a short “Enter/F2 to edit · changes saved on Import” hint. Update the manual with editing, bulk scope, reset, OCR conflict handling and optional columns. Preserve the dense default core columns.

finding: **The active Reports page contains neither live stage/progress nor Cancel.** It says only “Report operation in progress. Use Cancel in the progress window.” The other window is intentionally delayed by one second and can be behind another window; Home has the inline progress/cancel that Reports lacks. Do not infer that cancellation is wholly unavailable.
evidence: `04006_ImportWorkspace__running__light.png`, `04008_ImportWorkspace__running_import__light.png`/JSON `w37`; corresponding dark/150% states; `src/metroliza/ui/parsing_dialog.py:637–639, 904–916, 1327–1339`; `src/metroliza/ui/worker_progress_dialog.py:209–241`; `src/metroliza/ui/main_window.py:801–804`. Visible Reports-specific duck progress was not captured.
impact: Users waiting in the core workspace must locate a second surface or navigate to Home to check stage or stop. The current row statuses remain review statuses during import, adding no current-stage information.
recommendation: Put stage, processed/total, progress and cooperative Cancel in the existing Reports status region from operation start; after cancellation say “Stopping after current report; saved reports are retained.” Keep the delayed window as an optional shared detail surface and mirror the same state to Home.

finding: **Failures lose actionable explanation in the persistent surface.** Preflight failure ignores its detail and shows “Check the source and destination, then retry.” Embedded import stores the worker error but only changes the outcome title to Import failed; the explanatory error message is shown by the standalone completion branch, not the normal embedded one. Aggregate per-report failure counts likewise contain no repair reason.
evidence: `src/metroliza/ui/parser_preflight_worker.py:41–54`; `src/metroliza/ui/parsing_dialog.py:1030–1037, 1433–1437, 1460–1472, 1494–1499`. No failure screenshot exists. This concerns visible safe recovery guidance, not a request to display raw parser exceptions.
impact: Locked/unwritable destinations, missing sources and parse problems lead to undirected retries or log hunting. Users cannot tell what to change from the persistent result alone.
recommendation: Return bounded error categories and safe next actions, e.g. source unavailable, destination not writable/busy, parser failure, changed source. Bind them to relevant fields/report identities; offer Retry review or Open destination as appropriate. Preserve privacy sanitization and keep technical diagnostics secondary.

finding: **The explicit tab order omits details/outcome/path fields and downstream controls, producing a nonvisual cycle.** In the reviewed inventory, Tab from the table reaches OCR → Metadata → Import → database path → navigation → three downstream actions → Report details. Source/database paths have empty accessible names and no label-buddy binding in this constructor. Core actions/search have no shortcuts or mnemonics in the capture.
evidence: `04007_ImportWorkspace__review_planner__light.json` `focusChain`, `w18`, `w29`, `w33`; `04009_ImportWorkspace__done__light.json` `focusChain`; `src/metroliza/ui/parsing_dialog.py:521–538`; `src/metroliza/ui/report_planner.py:151, 168–188`; `src/metroliza/ui/ui_foundation.py:786–800`. Space/Enter/F2 are implemented and are not missing.
impact: Keyboard users need about nine forward Tab moves from the table to Report details in this captured cycle; the destination path is encountered far from its label/context. Native assistive naming remains unverified.
recommendation: Define one complete visual/workflow tab sequence including copyable paths, details/outcome toggles and downstream actions. Add nonconflicting documented review/import/search shortcuts, bind path labels/names, and provide a keyboard route to Columns. Verify Enter commits an edit without triggering import and Esc behaves safely on Windows.

finding: **Long paths show their common prefix and hide the actual database/workbook names.** The read-only fields deliberately move the cursor to character 0. With deep directories, source and destination therefore look almost identical; the basename summary that could compensate is below the fold. This is not a request to expand the window to fit full paths.
evidence: `shots/09006_ExportDialog__populated_output_selected__scale150.png` w9/w12; `shots/08006_ExportDialog__populated_output_selected__dark.png`; `ui/ui_foundation.py:786–800`, especially `setCursorPosition(0)`; `ui/export_dialog.py:1040–1063` places basename identities only in the separate summary.
impact: Makes confirmation of batch/database/output identity slower and more error-prone, particularly when an already-open Export keeps its context. Hover/cursor movement becomes necessary for a basic safety check.
recommendation: Keep bounded/copyable fields, but show the basename and enough trailing folders, with middle elision or a separate filename label. Retain full path on hover/copy and name each path accessibly.

finding: **Completion does not directly open the local workbook/dashboard, and its result actions disappear after acknowledgement.** The output list contains ordinary filesystem paths, but auto-linking recognizes only URI schemes. The only local result action reveals the primary file's folder; even a primary-file URI is handled as reveal. The parent then shows Ready for export rather than a last-result link. The manual describes local file links.
evidence: `shots/07010_QMessageBox__done_message__light.png` w0/w2/w5, `shots/08010_QMessageBox__done_message__dark.png`, `shots/07011_ExportDialog__done__light.png`; `exporting/export_outcomes.py:791–824`; `ui/export_dialog.py:101,117–138,159–173,191–207,1483–1529`; manual `docs/user_manual/export_overview.md:161–163,374–379`. Dashboard behavior follows the same code, without a grouped completion capture.
impact: Every daily review requires folder navigation and opening the file externally. After dismissing the message, finding the prior result requires reconstructing its location; grouped users cannot go straight to the dashboard they are meant to read first.
recommendation: Add explicit **Open workbook**, **Open dashboard** and **Show in folder** actions for completed artifacts. Persist a compact last-result row until the next run, with run status and those actions; preserve omission/diagnostic information.

finding: **Committed grouping is summarized only as Applied.** Export accepts the grouped dataframe but does not show custom-group names/count, assigned/default counts or scope. Its deliverables summary repeats only grouping on/off. This cannot distinguish an intended comparison from a different/mostly POPULATION assignment.
evidence: `ui/export_dialog.py:1234–1238,1278–1285,1054–1062`; `ui/data_grouping.py:2273–2280` returns the full copied frame. `shots/13006_DataGrouping__populated_group_2_added__light.png` demonstrates meaningful names and assigned/population counts in the child, not a captured committed parent state.
impact: Experts must reopen the editor to verify the grouping that controls the dashboard, adding a window transition and losing the final-at-a-glance check.
recommendation: Return a concise summary such as **2 custom groups · 24 assigned · 96 population**, with names and scope accessible on demand. Show **Group Analysis → HTML dashboard** visibly beside it. If later filter changes affect membership, mark the summary for recheck.

finding: **Only the selected preset survives closing the working window.** Routine changes such as Scatter, Sample # ordering, optional HTML and advanced overrides are not saved in the export config. The coordinator deletes closed windows, so reopening reconstructs defaults; dashboard appearance, by contrast, has separate persistence. Filters/groups need their existing safety reset, but output-style preferences need not be lost with them.
evidence: `ui/export_dialog.py:333–348,371–377,394–400,482–498,520–521,1373–1374`; `exporting/export_preset_utils.py:119–128` migrates config to only `selected_preset`; `ui/window_coordinator.py:200–209`; visual persistence `ui/dashboard_visual_options_dialog.py:263–267`. No reopen capture.
impact: Users who close Export between batches/days must repeat routine output choices and can miss an override they assumed was remembered. Remaining in the same open instance avoids this friction.
recommendation: Persist safe output/chart preferences or offer an explicit named export setup, visibly marking deviations from the base preset. Continue clearing data-specific scope on database changes; do not silently restore Google upload consent or data filters.

finding: Rename accepts an existing group name without collision validation. Renaming Lot A to Lot B rewrites A's members to B and overwrites the target group's colour; this is an implicit merge, including collisions involving the default group.
evidence: `data_grouping.py:2024–2037`. Exact source-extracted in-memory method probe: GROUP `[Lot A, Lot B, POPULATION]` became `[Lot B, Lot B, POPULATION]` after Rename A→B; no collision prompt is on this path.
impact: Distinct production lots can become one statistical population through a naming correction. There is no per-operation undo; restoring the draft may also discard other work.
recommendation: Trim/validate names and reject collisions for Rename. If merge is required, expose it as a separate deliberate action naming both groups and their member counts. Preserve default-group identity separately from its display name.

finding: Create or add chooses selected right-pane members only while that pane has focus. If both part panes have selections, moving focus to the shared action button makes the selector prefer the left Parts selection. The prompt identifies no target reports.
evidence: `data_grouping.py:1934–1950`, `1967–1982`, `728–730`; no focus policy preserving the right-pane ownership is configured in `499–524`. Exact source-extracted selector probe with both selections: right-pane focus returned `right-report`; action-button focus returned `left-report`. Native mouse routing remains untested.
impact: A mouse action can assign a different retained selection from the one the expert just reviewed, changing lot membership.
recommendation: Track the last active selection pane independently of current focus, or place explicit assignment actions in each pane. Before committing, show “Move N selected reports from [pane/group] to [target]”. Keyboard and mouse must use the same selection snapshot.

finding: Has NOK only selects reports with any NOK, not only NOK measurement rows. The visible label does not distinguish these levels, and the manual recommends it alongside Status=nok for rows with NOK results.
evidence: `10002_FilterDialog__populated__light.png` / JSON `w44`; `filter_dialog.py:274–278`, `1125`; `src/metroliza/reports/report_query_service.py:633–634`; `src/metroliza/reports/report_schema.py:284–288` distinguishes measurement `is_nok/status_code` from report `has_nok`; `docs/user_manual/export_filtering.md:252–253`.
impact: An expert following the NOK-row example can export OK measurements from failing reports, then spend time reconciling the unexpected rows. The report-level predicate itself is useful.
recommendation: Label the toggle “Reports with any NOK”. Expose “NOK measurements only” as the explicit measurement-status choice; explain the distinction in one short visible line and correct the manual example.

finding: SELECT ALL is a normal item inside multi-select lists. It can coexist with named values; Apply treats the entire dimension as unrestricted if the sentinel is among them. There is no exclusive-selection handler.
evidence: `filter_dialog.py:220–228`, `302–316`, `490–563`, `1097–1109`; list-selection helper does not enforce exclusivity. `10002_FilterDialog__populated__light.png` shows the sentinel but not a mixed selection.
impact: A user selecting all then selecting/searching a specific value may see that value highlighted while exporting the unrestricted dimension. Header's review list can also show the misleading mixed set.
recommendation: Use “All values” as a mutually exclusive state: choosing a value clears All, choosing All clears specific values. Make the active state and summary consistent; keep multi-selection of actual values.

finding: Parts and Members concatenate metadata into long single-line strings. File identity is offscreen in both panes at default and 150% sizes; source rows provide group membership only by background colour, which selection highlighting replaces.
evidence: `13006_DataGrouping__populated_group_2_added__light.png`, `14006_DataGrouping__populated_group_2_added__dark.png`, `15006_DataGrouping__populated_group_2_added__scale150.png`; JSON `w15/w25`: about 399/397 logical px wide, full sample labels include filenames. `data_grouping.py:1335–1379`, `1525–1546`, `1126–1132`, `1152–1156`.
impact: Daily verification of similar samples requires horizontal scrolling; selected rows lose the only direct source-pane cue to their current group. This increases lot-assignment errors and visual effort.
recommendation: Use compact table columns: Sample, Date, Part/Revision, Group and File, with user-resizable widths and a compact details area for less frequent metadata. Show Group text even when selected; keep colour as a secondary cue.

finding: “Saved grouping” is only the parent Export's in-memory frame. Fresh Export starts with no grouping, and its persisted config migration retains only selected_preset; there is no Save/Load grouping action for yesterday's assignments.
evidence: `data_grouping.py:1031–1049`, `2274–2279`; `export_dialog.py:333–347`, `353–377`; `src/metroliza/exporting/export_preset_utils.py:119–128`. Complete control creation/layout in `data_grouping.py:459–635` contains no grouping persistence controls.
impact: The requested restart-to-next-day journey requires rebuilding each lot and repeating member selection/name prompts, even for the same database. Reopening within one session is supported and should be preserved.
recommendation: Add explicit local Save grouping / Load grouping controls, bound to database/report identity. On load, show matched, missing and new-report counts before use. Do not silently assign new reports by label similarity.

finding: Reference/Parts/Members previews truncate to 1,000 rows before the per-pane search is applied. That search only hides instantiated items. A matching item beyond the preview cannot be retrieved with Search, despite the marker's “Narrow the filter/search” advice.
evidence: `data_grouping.py:129`, `1509–1547`, `1673–1682`, `1758–1802`; `src/metroliza/shared/list_selection_utils.py:123–137`. Captured fixture is below the boundary; no screenshot reproduction claimed.
impact: Larger datasets require discovering the separate Filter rows expression workaround; a known reference/report can appear absent from the list search.
recommendation: Apply search to the full indexed dataset before limiting/paging, or use a model-backed paged view. Keep a bounded display and show “1,000 of N shown”; reference-level bulk actions must state whether they target displayed or all matching reports.

finding: The manual says the dialog has Clear grouping, which closes and clears applied grouping. The actual footer has Reset changes, which restores the last applied draft and stays open. These actions have different consequences.
evidence: `13006_DataGrouping__populated_group_2_added__light.png` / JSON `w33–w35`; `data_grouping.py:510–511`, `733–737`, `880–899`; `docs/user_manual/export_grouping.md:194–198`, `258`. Actual parent clear action: `export_dialog.py:1270–1274`; legacy `dont_use_grouping` is not the footer's connected handler.
impact: An expert following the manual cannot find the described action and may reset edits while still exporting the previously applied grouping.
recommendation: Align the manual with Reset changes and direct users to Export's Clear grouping action. State the distinction between resetting an unapplied draft and clearing the applied export context.

finding: Import CSV immediately upserts existing alias/scope keys, replacing their common names without a comparison or replacement count. The completion message only says how many rows were imported. Duplicate checking protects duplicates within the CSV, not replacement of existing database rules.
evidence: `U/characteristic_mapping_dialog.py:1198–1228,1314–1343`; `R/characteristic_alias_service.py:463–520,589–631`; `M/characteristic_name_matching.md:180–205`. No CSV operation screenshot exists for A5.
impact: Loading a shared or older CSV can silently alter how later Group Analysis combines/labels measurements.
recommendation: Validate first, then show Added / Replaced / Unchanged with old→new names and scopes; require explicit acceptance of replacements. Preserve atomic import and provide an export/backup action in the review.

finding: The stored-data editor has no visible selected database identity or load/empty explanation. Its footer offers only Select DB file, Cancel and Apply. Empty/no-DB/no-search-result pages look like blank tables. The matching manager already demonstrates the missing context pattern.
evidence: `S/16001_ModifyDB__initial__light.png`, `S/16002_ModifyDB__populated__light.png`, `S/18002_ModifyDB__populated__scale150.png`; inventories have no path/status widget. `U/modify_db.py:193–244,286–340,928–938`; compare `U/characteristic_mapping_dialog.py:537–545,702–728`.
impact: Users must infer the job from data or return to the owner window, especially after choosing a different DB; a blank grid gives no immediate recovery step.
recommendation: Add a compact read-only database path row, report/measurement counts and specific no DB / empty DB / no matches / load failed messages. Include target identity in review and completion.

finding: Selecting an existing path without lowercase `.db` changes the filename: `job.sqlite` becomes `job.sqlite.db`, and `job.DB` becomes `job.DB.db`. The resulting load targets a different file; schema preparation can create that file. Matching accepts `.db`, `.sqlite`, `.sqlite3` without rewriting. This concerns Browse, not construction with an already-selected `.sqlite` DB.
evidence: `U/modify_db.py:474–495,573–587`; `U/characteristic_mapping_dialog.py:730–743`. Populated fixtures use `.sqlite`, but the captured main-window path bypasses this ModifyDB chooser; there is no screenshot reproduction.
impact: A user reopening a valid report database can receive an empty grid or work on an unintended sibling file.
recommendation: Keep the exact selected existing filename; use the shared SQLite extensions in the filter and validate the selected database before replacing the current context. Never append an extension in an Open dialog.

finding: Record grids make identification and editing compete for width. Report labels visibly truncate (SAMPLE_NUMBER, OPERATOR_NAME, TEMPLATE_VARIANT); COMMENT is squeezed to a sliver. Measurement rows show 17 columns, repeated truncated feature text and only internal REPORT_ID context; MEAS/status require horizontal scrolling. There is no selected-report→measurements action or dedicated exact report filter.
evidence: `S/16004_ModifyDB__populated_tab1_2_Report_records__light.png` / JSON `w6` (11 columns, 120 rows); `S/16005_ModifyDB__populated_tab1_3_Measurement_rows__light.png` / JSON `w6` (17 columns, 17,280 rows). `U/modify_db.py:71–108,303–315,628–659,886–912`; `U/ui_foundation.py:803–825`.
impact: Repeated ID lookup, context switching and horizontal scrolling slow correction of a measurement in a known report and make adjacent rows harder to distinguish.
recommendation: Add “Measurements for selected report”; keep report reference/sample/file in a compact context strip. Freeze identity columns, choose initial widths by meaning, and offer remembered column visibility/order. Keep direct grid editing.

finding: No visible changed-cell indicator, pending count, changed-only view or per-cell revert exists. Apply is enabled merely because a DB is present. With no edits it opens an empty confirmation and only after OK reports No changes. The internal Undo button is outside the layout and is not a usable recovery feature.
evidence: `S/16002_ModifyDB__populated__light.png` / JSON `w22` enabled; `U/modify_db.py:233–244,327–328,940–992,1081–1083`; `U/modify_db_records.py:155–198` handles no dirty styling role; `M/modify_database.md:250–252`.
impact: Experts reviewing corrections across tabs cannot quickly distinguish pending work or revert just one mistake; no-op Apply costs an unnecessary two-dialog loop.
recommendation: Show “N pending changes” and changed-cell markers with textual/accessibility equivalents; enable Apply only for valid pending edits. Add changed-only view and Revert selected; retain the existing conservative discard guard.

finding: Bulk rename is available only through Enter/Return on selected normalization rows; the visible grid has no Rename selected action, shortcut hint or selected-row count. The manual carries the essential instruction.
evidence: `S/16002_ModifyDB__populated__light.png`, `S/16007_ModifyDB__populated_tab2_2_SAMPLE_NUMBER__light.png`, `S/16008_ModifyDB__populated_tab2_3_HEADER__light.png`; `U/modify_db.py:286–340,418–472`; `M/modify_database.md:148–175`.
impact: Users who do not know the shortcut repeat cell edits; experienced users cannot see the selection extent before triggering a broad rename.
recommendation: Add a compact **Rename selected… (Enter)** button beside a selection/occurrence count; keep Enter and Shift-range selection. Make global scope visible beside the action.

finding: The single search controls only report/export source names. Saved name matches have no search/filter or sorting enabled by this dialog. A growing ruleset must be inspected by scrolling, even when the expert knows its alias, common name or reference.
evidence: `S/19003_CharacteristicMappingDialog__populated__light.png` / JSON `w24` source search, `w10` saved table; `U/characteristic_mapping_dialog.py:543–574,638,867–929`; `U/ui_foundation.py:803–825`.
impact: Recurring maintenance of reference-specific rules becomes slower and increases the chance of overlooking an existing rule. Actual large-ruleset frequency is a PO question, not measured here.
recommendation: Add “Search saved matches” across original/common/reference plus an All scopes filter; preserve selected rule and scroll position after edits.

finding: Save is enabled with required fields empty and uses modal warnings. Duplicate alias/scope validation occurs in the manager after the editor accepts and closes; rejection loses the open editing context instead of identifying the conflicting rule in place.
evidence: `S/22001_CharacteristicAliasEditorDialog__initial__light.png` / JSON `w13` enabled and default; `U/characteristic_mapping_dialog.py:392–408,467–496,989–1007,1031–1054`.
impact: A missing field interrupts the form; a duplicate match requires reopening and re-entering intended changes instead of correcting the current entry.
recommendation: Disable Save for missing required fields with inline reasons. Check uniqueness before closing; show the existing match and offer “Edit existing” while retaining the entered replacement/scope.

finding: Important search fields, tables, combos and the loading bar lack explicit accessible names/descriptions; editor labels have no buddy connections or mnemonics. Neither file defines tab order. The manager's inventory focus chain visits both tables before database/search controls, contrary to the visible top-to-bottom task sequence. Button text alone is not evidence of a missing button name; the concern is the unlabeled data controls and navigation.
evidence: `S/16004_ModifyDB__populated_tab1_2_Report_records__light.json` `w5/w6`; `S/19003_CharacteristicMappingDialog__populated__light.json` `focusChain`, `w1/w10/w24`; `S/22005_CharacteristicAliasEditorDialog__populated__light.json` `w3/w7/w11/w13`; `S/100001_RecordBusyBanner__running__light.json` `w3`. `U/modify_db.py:193–244,286–370`; `U/characteristic_mapping_dialog.py:359–408,537–662`; `U/modify_db_records.py:328–341`; helper exists at `U/ui_foundation.py:828–832`.
impact: Keyboard users spend extra navigation steps; assistive-technology users may not receive the field/table purpose reliably. Actual Windows announcements remain unverified.
recommendation: Register explicit names/descriptions and label buddies; define task-ordered tab chains and sensible initial focus. Add mnemonics for frequent actions and a named progress status. Validate with Windows keyboard and screen-reader runs.

finding: Applying limits for a temporary metric subset deletes saved limits for deselected metrics. Reproduction by code: set limits for A and B → choose A only → open/apply Limits → reselect B. The dialog contains only A and returns only A; the parent replaces its entire map. B falls back to the original candidate limits, usually none for file metrics.
evidence: `UI:1983–1994` passes only `_selected_metrics()` and assigns `self.metric_spec_limits = dialog.limits()`; `589–604,624–628` builds a new subset map; `2236–2246,2286–2303` keeps candidate items and uses map-or-candidate fallback. No captured transition; `97003` shows the subset-only editor structure.
impact: A routine selection edit can silently change later specification-based analysis. The main metric count does not warn that B's manual limits disappeared.
recommendation: Merge results only for fields edited in this dialog; represent an explicit cleared limit separately from an omitted metric. Retain inactive metrics' specifications and show a manual-limit count in the launcher.

finding: Correcting Time column, Part / ID column or Excel sheet immediately destroys selected metrics, manual limits, filters and groups. The reload notice explains reloading, not the lost setup. Reload populates all detected metrics again.
evidence: `UI:1486–1514,1908–1933,2236–2246`; `25006`/`27006` place these editable mapping controls above the configured analysis. No transition capture.
impact: An expert fixing interpretation late in the process must repeat setup and can overlook that all numeric columns are selected again.
recommendation: Keep stale-data protection, but retain a draft recipe; revalidate/reapply compatible selections and limits after reload, with a visible list of dropped mappings. Warn before discarding assignments that cannot survive.

finding: There is no analysis preset or reapply-last-setup control. A new input clears source-dependent configuration and resets output paths; reopening constructs a fresh dialog. Dashboard visual settings are loaded separately, so saving a visual recipe does not save the analysis setup.
evidence: `UI:644–695,757–820,1720–1758`; `main_window.py:1211–1219`; constructors/control/handler inspection finds no analysis-preset serialization or UI. Main `25001`/`25006` expose no such control.
impact: Same-schema daily files require repeat metric/limit/filter/group work. Keeping the window open preserves only some choices; users must remember which ones survive.
recommendation: Add named analysis recipes and Reapply last setup, schema-bound with explicit review of missing/changed fields. Store filter/group rules where representable, never blindly carry row assignments to a new dataset. Show recipe state and output naming policy.

finding: On the populated default window, Advanced's toggle and the readiness explanation lie below the viewport while Create remains fixed and visible. Invalid-state reasons can therefore be spatially detached from the disabled action.
evidence: `25006` and `27006` PNGs visibly end at the Advanced heading; inventories: viewport `w3=[14,33,838,587]`, toggle `w41=[14,626,838,36]`, readiness `w42=[14,670,838,45]`; `UI:1054–1077` puts readiness inside the scroller and actions outside. This is confirmed visually despite toggle's false-negative clipped flag.
impact: Workbook/tuning need an extra scroll; a disabled Create may require searching below the fold for its reason. This occurs with the short fixture, before long headers.
recommendation: Move readiness beside the fixed footer; reduce redundant source rows and put mapping controls in a compact aligned row. Keep one Advanced toggle visible above the scroller's lower edge or in its own stable row.

finding: Long input/dashboard paths display the leading directory prefix and hide the filename. The bounded field is safe, but the routinely useful distinguishing portion is absent from the scan path.
evidence: `25006`, `26006`, `27006`; inventory `w10` input and `w38` dashboard show long common prefixes; `UI:2377–2386`; `ui_foundation.py:786–800` uses a read-only field and always positions the cursor at zero.
impact: Comparing today's source/output name with yesterday's requires tooltip, keyboard scrolling or copying; the destination basename cannot be checked at a glance.
recommendation: Show filename plus a middle-elided directory or a separate folder line; retain full-path tooltip/copy. Name the dashboard/workbook path fields for assistive technology.

finding: Option dialogs omit the key distinction that statistics/workbooks use all selected rows while chart points may be sampled or made noninteractive. Static-layer hover/selection loss and threshold units are absent. The interactivity dialog supports a selected-row notice, but its actual caller never supplies row_count. Group thresholds remain editable in every mode.
evidence: `88003`, `91003` and JSON controls/text; `UI:169–176,183–217,240–244,274–325,1435–1439,1452–1456`; manual §5 explicitly explains all-row statistics and static-layer interaction loss.
impact: Users cannot confidently predict why charts have fewer points or no hover, or whether threshold edits matter in a forced mode, without leaving for the manual.
recommendation: Show current selected rows and a short mode-dependent outcome: “Charts: up to 50,000 visual rows; statistics/workbook: all N rows”; “Static layers have no hover/point selection.” Label thresholds in rows and disable them outside Auto. Pass effective filtered row count.

finding: Search hides nonmatching metrics, but Select all and Clear iterate over every item, including hidden ones. Labels provide no scope distinction or matching-count feedback.
evidence: `94003` displays search + generic bulk actions; `UI:470–476` loops the whole list; `485–493` only hides items. Filtered bulk operation not captured.
impact: Clearing a searched family can also remove unrelated hidden selections; restoring the intended subset requires rescanning and can change output coverage.
recommendation: Provide Select matching/Clear matching when a search is active; retain an explicitly labeled All metrics action if needed. Show matching count and total selected count together.

finding: Important data editors lack explicit accessible names: metric search/list and limits table. The launcher names many controls but leaves output path fields unnamed. No action shortcuts/mnemonics are defined for repeated filter/metrics/limits/group navigation.
evidence: `94003.json`: `w3` search and `w4` list names empty; `97003.json`: `w3` table name empty; `25006.json`: `w38` path name empty and buttons have empty shortcuts; `UI:375–431,510–565,1174–1224`. Native button text can still provide button names; no blanket screen-reader failure is asserted.
impact: Assistive users receive weaker editor context; keyboard experts traverse multiple path/combo/action stops for common edits. Actual screen-reader announcement behavior requires Windows verification.
recommendation: Name search, metric checklist, limits table and output fields; associate editor descriptions with purpose/scope; add a small consistent mnemonic/shortcut set and explicitly maintain focus order as layout changes.

finding: Completion links and counts exist only in a modal message. Dismissing it returns to an indistinguishable ready-to-run configuration; no last-run artifact link, scope summary or outcome remains. The success message also uses a full URI as link text.
evidence: `25009` links/counts followed by `25010` with configuration only; `UI:353–369,2755–2783,2469–2474`; `export_dialog_service.py:208–216` builds full-URI artifact text.
impact: An expert who dismisses success must locate the output externally or risk rerunning to recover context. Full URI wrapping obscures artifact identity during the brief completion step.
recommendation: Retain a compact Last run row with time, row/metric counts, actual artifact basenames, Open dashboard/Open workbook/Open folder and outcome. Keep copyable full paths and optional detailed message.

finding: **Confirming an unchanged filter discards all applied groups.** Every Accepted return calls `_clear_tabular_grouping()`; there is no old/new filter comparison or impact confirmation. This clears assignments and turns groupstats off. Example: build 12 groups, reopen Filter rows just to inspect it, click Apply without editing; grouping is now absent.
evidence: `IA:1839–1847` unconditional clear; `IA:1516–1520` clears snapshot/data/applied flag and groupstats. `TF:1008–1019` permits acceptance without a change. S-CSV shows the starting combination of All rows and 12 groups; transition is not captured.
impact: A routine confirm action can cost minutes of regrouping and silently change downstream cohort statistics/charts. Losing groups after a real scope change may be a policy choice; losing them on a no-op is avoidable.
recommendation: Compare canonical accepted filter state first and preserve groups on no-op. Before a real scope change that invalidates groups, show the concrete impact and offer Cancel or an explicit reset/reconcile action. Keep groupstats state truthful.

finding: **Membership cannot be audited reliably in the row-store path.** The member list shows only `Row N`, although source Part/ID is detected. Its rows are built with blank reference/date/part/file fields. Both backends cap members at the first 1,000 without member search or paging; only the selector pane has paging. The capture demonstrates the weak identity; the >1,000 limit is source-only.
evidence: S-GP/S-G150 JSON `w19`: `Row 1`, `Row 13`, etc.; S-CSV detects Part/ID `PART`. `TG:1300–1347,2331–2407,1672–1679`; limit `TG:86–87`; layout `TG:450–462`. Contrast S-DBG and `DG:490–497,1335–1373`, which expose member search and metrology context.
impact: A user must cross-reference row numbers outside this dialog to validate/correct membership. Members beyond the preview cap cannot be found for individual removal here. Large multi-file inputs make provenance especially important.
recommendation: Add a bounded searchable/paged member model with source file/sheet, source row, Part/ID and relevant selector values. Keep the true total and visible-range count next to the list; fetch context only for visible rows. Avoid loading all rows to solve this.

finding: **Remove individual rows is an invisible keyboard-only action.** A real removal handler is wired to Delete/Backspace, but the dialog has no Remove from group button, context action or visible shortcut hint. `Clear selection` only clears matching-selector selection; it does not remove members. The database flow exposes the same correction as a button.
impact: A user who misassigns a few rows may recreate a group or reset the whole session because the available recovery appears to be Delete group. Mouse users have no visible individual-removal route.
recommendation: Put `Remove from group` beneath the member pane, enabled for selected custom-group members. Keep Delete/Backspace as the shortcut and show it in a compact context menu/hint; preserve distinct Delete group confirmation.

finding: **Adding a selector column requires a double-click without a keyboard-equivalent command.** Unlike the neighboring CSV filter, no Add/Remove controls appear. Available columns are not passed to the shared Enter handler and no itemActivated binding adds them. Use grouping is the default button, so it is unsafe to assume Enter on an available column means Add. Actual key propagation was not executed.
evidence: S-GP `w10/w14`, footer `w42–w49`; inventory `w49` default=true/autoDefault=true. `TG:518–521,566–582,1448–1469,2435–2458`; `LS:195–216` has no available-column branch. Filter equivalent `TF:240–248,317–323`. Manual `MAN:137–139` documents double-click only.
impact: Daily keyboard users must reach for the mouse during selector setup; occasional users must recover the gesture from the manual. Similar-looking column choosers teach different actions.
recommendation: Add compact Add/Remove controls and explicit Enter/itemActivated handling on available columns, with Delete on selected columns. Keep double-click as the expert shortcut. Define tab order as search → corresponding list → transfer action.

finding: **Clear values also removes the selected column's date constraint.** The button and accessible name refer only to selected values; `clear_selection()` additionally calls date storage with force_clear=True, which resets mode to Any date and clears both bounds. It is even enabled for a date-only condition.
evidence: S-FP footer `w24` label/name; `TF:299–305,493–499,971–978,1076–1079`. Active date controls are not captured.
impact: Clearing categorical selections can unexpectedly broaden a carefully chosen date range. The user must notice a changed row count and reconstruct the dates.
recommendation: Have Clear values clear only selected values, and offer a separate clear-date action; alternatively label it `Clear column condition` and describe the exact scope visibly. Keep Reset filter as the whole-draft action.

finding: **The column chooser receives too little height for the first task.** At 1060×720, both column lists are only 60 logical pixels high, showing roughly four rows; the empty values list occupies 231 pixels. Advanced expression, two search rows and transfer controls consume the upper budget. This is poor space allocation rather than a clipping-flag defect.
evidence: S-FP JSON `w10/w14`: `[14,215,511,60]` / `[535,215,511,60]`, 11 available rows; `w22`: height 231. `TF:188–199,208–265` stacks the regions and weights columns 1 / values 2. Constructor minima are declared at `TF:224–227,262`, but the inventory's effective list minima are 30; shared QSS sets list min-height at `UF:227–237`. Exact Windows behavior/root cause is unverified.
impact: Users scroll the field picker repeatedly even with only 11 source columns. Long condition summaries have little room; the simulated smaller laptop cannot be assumed to improve this allocation.
recommendation: Use a horizontal split: compact column/condition region on the left and the active column's values/date region on the right. Preserve practical post-theme list minima, allow splitter resizing, and place advanced expression below the routine selectors. Verify the actual Windows 150% layout.

finding: **The manual teaches combinations while the controls implement independent column conditions.** Section 2 describes selecting `TraceCode`/`Batch` value combinations; the UI selects one column's values at a time and ANDs columns. Selecting TraceCode A,B and Batch 1,2 admits every existing cross-pair, not just A/1 and B/2. The same section also calls the expression control Magic filter, a name absent from the captured dialog.
evidence: `MAN:107–119`; S-FP column/value regions and Advanced expression label `w4`; `TF:405–419,443–456,1097–1116` shows per-column selected-values masks intersected across columns. `TF:188–190` names the expression. Tuple selection belongs to grouping (`MAN:137–149`), not this visual filter. Cross-pair consequence is derived from code, not a captured result.
impact: An expert following the manual can misunderstand the analyzed row population or spend time looking for a missing Magic filter control. The row count alone does not explain the boolean relationship.
recommendation: Document `OR within a column; AND between columns; advanced expression also restricts rows`. Put a short equivalent condition summary near Apply. Use Advanced expression consistently. Explain how explicit OR-of-paired predicates selects non-rectangular combinations; do not silently change the current filtering semantics.

finding: The sample silently stops at four comparison groups and always includes a population sample. Its element selector is built from that sample, so later real groups cannot be individually inspected/selected before export. No sample/count qualifier explains the omission.
evidence: V-ready/V-custom show G-000…G-003; V-custom JSON `w82` enumerates only those groups and sample means; C/BG-long show 12 groups. `src/metroliza/charts/dashboard_visual_options.py:79`, `:732`, `:761`, `:901`; `src/metroliza/ui/dashboard_visual_options_dialog.py:325`, `:638`.
impact: An expert configuring G-004…G-011 must export first to check/edit them in the browser; that is too late for colours baked into static layers. A four-group example cannot validate a dense-group recipe for the actual selection.
recommendation: Keep a lightweight synthetic sample, label it **Style sample — 4 of 12 groups**, and provide a searchable all-group style list plus preview subset selector. Make population conditional or clearly identify it as a sample baseline.

finding: Theme Delete writes to disk immediately without confirmation/undo; Cancel does not restore it. Save/Update also write immediately, and Update with Current settings creates a theme rather than being unavailable. The UI gives no separate library-save status or transaction boundary.
evidence: V-ready JSON `w7=Current settings`, enabled `w11–w13` and footer Cancel; `src/metroliza/ui/dashboard_visual_options_dialog.py:817`, `:832`, `:851`, `:537`; disk writer `src/metroliza/charts/dashboard_visual_options.py:460`.
impact: A mistaken delete/update can remove a reusable house style and is not recoverable by cancelling the dialog. Enabled no-target actions and identical emphasis make the expected operation less predictable.
recommendation: Stage library changes until Apply, or explicitly label immediate library actions and offer undo/confirmation for deletion/replacement. Disable Update/Delete without a saved target; use **Save as…**, **Update theme**, **Delete theme** and a short saved/pending status.

window: Dashboard interactivity; Large group layers; CSV options
finding: Setup exposes sampling, chart-size fallback and static layers as separate technical knobs without a combined explanation of hover/point-marking/colour consequences. The available selected-row notice is never given `row_count` by the parent. All rows can still lose interactivity to the finite size cap; static layers cannot support per-point selection or later recolouring.
evidence: I/L show the full forms and their notes; `src/metroliza/ui/industrial_analytics_dialog.py:172`, `:215`, `:310`, `:1435`, `:1431`; fallback/layer selection in `src/metroliza/industrial/industrial_analytics_dashboard.py:381`, `:393`, `:720`; intended limits in `docs/user_manual/csv_summary.md:200` and `:237`.
impact: A reviewer can request every point or tune a style, wait for generation, then discover that the required Find point/mark/recolour task is unavailable on image layers and needs a changed setup plus regeneration. No large-input occurrence was timed here.
recommendation: Pass current filtered-row context; show a concise consequence summary before Apply/start: statistical scope, plotted-row/sample scope, layer mode, and **Hover/point marks: interactive layers only; image colours fixed at export**. State that a finite budget can replace charts with snapshots even in All rows. Add point units/chart scope to thresholds.

finding: Customize opens into a mostly disabled Advanced palette/Series block on the default recipe, with no inline reason or **Edit as Custom** action. Editing a raw swatch requires Custom recipe + Fixed palette + Custom swatches. The faster group-chip route selects an inspector target but does not reveal that inspector when customization is collapsed.
evidence: V-ready shows chips with customization hidden; V-custom JSON `w31`, `w33`, `w35`, `w37–w48` disabled. `src/metroliza/ui/dashboard_visual_options_dialog.py:335`, `:568`, `:708`, `:730`, `:878`, `:1138`; the chip handler has no expansion action and `_build_controls` has no visible prerequisite text.
impact: The expert who needs one mandated group/brand colour encounters either locked fields or a chip action whose result is hidden, then must infer mode dependencies or consult the manual.
recommendation: Let a group-chip action reveal and focus its inspector. Offer **Edit a copy as Custom** while preserving the resolved look; label chips **Edit group style**. When controls are locked, show the exact reason and one enabling action.

finding: Browser style/theme/point-mark changes use localStorage, but the controls do not state that they are local to that browser/dashboard rather than saved into the shared HTML or desktop library. Storage failures are silently ignored.
evidence: B-long/BG-long show inline Find point/Mark selected without persistence-scope text; modal/control markup `src/metroliza/charts/dashboard_html_controls.py:685`, `:728`, `:3320`; storage and ignored errors `:1542`, `:1644`, `:1665`; expected local-only behavior `docs/user_manual/dashboard_visuals.md`, “Marking Individual Points.”
impact: A metrologist can hand off an HTML expecting a colleague to see a highlighted sample or house style; the later local annotations do not travel with the file. Retention is also uncertain if browser storage is unavailable.
recommendation: Add **Review marks and changes are saved in this browser only** beside marking/Visuals, with a saved/unavailable indicator. Preserve the current local-only data contract. If portable review state is wanted, scope an explicit export/import action separately.
effort: S for scope/status; M for optional portable state

finding: The 15 fixed filters and advanced-expression editor are placed in one vertical layout without a scroll area. The captured full dialog is 720×870 logical px; the shared sizing helper caps windows to available screen geometry. At a 1280×720 logical work area the full form cannot remain at its captured height, so controls compete for height and may require manual resizing or risk being below the visible area. The scale150 state was not captured, so this is a code-based target-size concern.
evidence: `64002_IndustrialAnalyticsFilterDialog__populated__light.png` and inventory (720×870); `src/metroliza/ui/industrial_analytics_filter_dialog.py:119-161`; sizing cap in `src/metroliza/ui/ui_foundation.py:604-646`
impact: On a laptop work area, reaching lower fixed fields or Apply may require repeated resizing/scroll workaround; users can lose sight of the commit action while scanning filters.
recommendation: Keep the summary and action row fixed; put the long fixed-field form and advanced expressions in a scrollable body. Consider visually grouping time/source filters from part/production identifiers.

finding: The manual directs users to a “connection-check action in the source setup,” but the source editor has no test/check control; its available actions are New source, Close and Save source. The actual **Check access** action is in the separate Fetch industrial data dialog.
evidence: `46002_IndustrialSourceProfilesDialog__populated__light.png`; `docs/user_manual/industrial_data.md:72-74`; `src/metroliza/ui/industrial_source_profiles_dialog.py:113-145,556-565`; `src/metroliza/ui/industrial_sync_dialog.py:356-387`
impact: Experts may search the setup form for a nonexistent check before discovering they must save, return, open fetch, and check there. This adds a detour before a production fetch.
recommendation: Align the manual with the actual two-step sequence (“Save source, then open Fetch to cache and choose Check access”). Keep the source editor’s saved-state handoff consistent with that wording.

finding: The multi-line Signal columns editor is only 30 logical pixels high in the captured Setup view, displaying roughly one mapping line at a time. This conflicts with its multi-line syntax and intended 96-pixel minimum, making review and editing of several signals slower and easier to misread.
evidence: `67004_RealtimeIndustrialMonitoringDialog__populated_tab1_2_Setup__light.png`; inventory `w` Signal columns / `QPlainTextEdit`, geometry height 30, versus `realtime_industrial_monitoring_dialog.py:306-308`; scrollable setup at `:236-256`
impact: Operators configuring multiple signals cannot scan the configured mappings together and must scroll within a cramped field while the whole form also scrolls.
recommendation: Preserve a visibly multi-line editor (at least three mapping lines) and check its effective height at the minimum window size and 150% laptop layout. Keep advanced settings collapsed by default, and make the source-save action easy to reach.

finding: After creating a handoff folder, Check Package, Validate, Diagnose, Repair Prompt and Install all become enabled together. Install therefore looks like a peer/next action before the manual’s package-check and review sequence. The install backend does revalidate, so this is a misleading workflow cue rather than a confirmed unsafe install path.
evidence: `76002_ParserPluginWizardDialog__populated__light.png`; inventory Install enabled; `parser_plugin_wizard.py:206-216,236-249`; manual `docs/user_manual/parser_profiles.md` “Check Package”, “Validate”, “Diagnose”, “Install”; install routine revalidates at `parsing/declarative_parser_profiles.py:1199-1205`
impact: Users can skip the visible package integrity check and any needed parser-selection diagnosis, or waste time clicking Install before inputs are ready and receiving an error.
recommendation: Reflect readiness in the action states: allow Check Package first, Validate once inputs exist, and Install only after package and validation pass; surface Diagnose as the indicated review step where selection ambiguity requires it. Keep the backend validation as the final guard.

finding: Brak jakichkolwiek skrótów klawiszowych i mnemoników Alt (0 × QShortcut/setShortcut/QKeySequence/StandardKey, 0 × '&' w etykietach); tylko lokalne Enter/Spacja/Delete/F2 w 6 oknach.
evidence: grep w src/metroliza; main_window.py:436–503
recommendation: Mały, sprawdzony pod kątem kolizji zestaw skrótów (Ctrl+1…7, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+F, F1) i mnemoniki Alt.

finding: Brak listy ostatnich baz, folderów i plików; okno główne nie ma menu File (menu: Tools, View, Help). Każda sesja zaczyna się od okien wyboru plików.
