finding: The default opens the first reference block; no cross-reference exception index or internal navigation exists. Each reference spans 360 columns for 72 metrics; the raw table is last.
evidence: O1 `workbook-inventory.json`: `out-export_run/export.xlsx`, active `REF001`, 38 sheets, 0 internal links; `src/metroliza/exporting/export_data_thread.py:5265`, `:5299`, `:5403`, `:6088`; `src/metroliza/exporting/export_preset_utils.py:15` disables extended summaries for Main plots.
impact: An expert who does not already know the suspect characteristic must scan blocks/sheets or build a raw-data filter every day. Actual time cost was not measured.
recommendation: Add a compact opening index with source/scope, observed NOK count, characteristic/reference rows sorted by attention, and internal links; retain all current reference/raw sheets.

finding: Group comparison emits every metric as an undifferentiated navigation chip. The opening overview counts sections/charts/group metrics rather than surfacing which metrics need attention. There is no searchable or risk-filtered metric index.
evidence: Main writer only; no main Group HTML was retained; `src/metroliza/charts/export_html_dashboard.py:3015`, `:4297`, `:4607`; `src/metroliza/charts/dashboard_navigation.py:33` uses wrapping chips; `:4635` places the full metric list before metric content.
impact: Large exports require visual/name searches before the expert can reach NOK/restricted/warning-heavy characteristics; many anchors also lengthen keyboard traversal.
recommendation: A compact metric table/search with reference, metric, observed NOK, restriction/warning and next action; default attention-first sorting and stable direct links. Keep visible overall analysis status.

finding: CSV workbook data/aggregate/metric/parameter tables are exported without frozen headers, filters or fitted table widths; numeric summaries largely use General formatting. Core Export already supplies frozen/filterable raw data.
evidence: O1 supplemental workbook inventory; `src/metroliza/tabular/tabular_analytics_service.py:4654`, `:4663`, `:4683`, `:4687`; only the chart sheet sets widths at `src/metroliza/industrial/industrial_analytics_workbook_charts.py:92`; contrast `src/metroliza/exporting/export_data_thread.py:6104`, `:6190`.
impact: Every fresh workbook requires setup before sorting/filtering thousands of rows; headers disappear during scrolling and numeric precision is harder to scan.
recommendation: Reuse a shared worksheet table policy: freeze first row, filters, bounded content widths, appropriate date/metric precision, summary-first navigation; preserve all underlying values.

finding: The saved dashboard relies on companion assets, but completion presents the HTML as a file without a visible keep-assets-together instruction or a portable-package action.
evidence: O1 `html-inventory.json` relative asset references; `src/metroliza/charts/export_html_dashboard.py:641`, `:708`; `src/metroliza/industrial/industrial_analytics_dashboard.py:340`, `:490`; `src/metroliza/exporting/export_outcomes.py:791`; `src/metroliza/ui/industrial_analytics_dialog.py:351`; manual `export_overview.md`, “HTML dashboard”, explicitly warns to keep the matching assets.
impact: Sending/moving just the visible HTML can remove external snapshots or interactive runtime for the recipient; embedded CSV snapshots survive, but its Plotly script is external. A manual-only warning is easy to miss at handoff.
recommendation: Display a short packaging note beside **Open dashboard** and provide **Save sharing package (.zip)** containing HTML and its exact referenced assets.

finding: CSV dashboards identify the source and row scope but do not display a generation timestamp or data-through timestamp. Main Export already has shared snapshot metadata.
evidence: O1 `html-inventory.json`: both CSV dashboard headers; `src/metroliza/industrial/industrial_analytics_dashboard.py:3907`, `:5547`; compare `src/metroliza/charts/export_html_dashboard.py:3006` and `src/metroliza/charts/dashboard_html_controls.py:172`.
impact: A shared dashboard with the same source basename is hard to distinguish from yesterday's snapshot without inspecting filesystem metadata or chart dates.
recommendation: Reuse the existing saved-snapshot metadata: **Generated**, **Data through**, selected range, and an explicit unknown state when timestamps are unavailable; never imply live freshness.

window: MainWindow Home and Reports output handoff
finding: Home's “next action” never becomes Export after a successful import: every idle branch leads back to Reports review/import. In the successful Reports capture, Review remains primary while Export is a secondary bottom peer.
evidence: `04009_ImportWorkspace__done__light.png`: Import successful, Review reports accent, Export Workbook secondary; `01005_MainWindow__populated__light.png` shows the report-oriented Home action. `main_window.py:772–807,607,1131–1135,234–237`; Home post-success behavior is source-traced, not separately captured.
impact: Returning to Home after import adds a second launch click and recommends repeating preparation instead of the usual next output step. Direct Reports→Export remains one click.
recommendation: Keep Reports' direct action. On a verified successful import or an opened existing database, offer a clearly labeled Export Workbook action on Home, with Review/import available beside it. Do not infer readiness from a selected path alone or bypass export validation.

finding: The same report-database concept appears as Database file and Select DB file; workbook destinations switch between Excel file and Output workbook. Normalization tabs and filter actions retain ALL CAPS while peer controls use sentence case.
evidence: `04009_ImportWorkspace__done__light.png`; `16002_ModifyDB__populated__light.png`; `07002_ExportDialog__populated__light.png`; `10002_FilterDialog__populated__light.png`; `58002_IndustrialExportDialog__populated__light.png`. `modify_db.py:234,299–301`; `export_dialog.py:433`; `industrial_export_dialog.py:228`; `filter_dialog.py:303–316`.
impact: Small recurring translation cost between screens; new source types make abbreviated DB wording less precise. No PL/EN defect was verified.
recommendation: Use “Database file” for report databases and distinguish “Industrial cache” explicitly; use “Output workbook” for .xlsx destinations. Use sentence case for user-facing tabs/actions while preserving real schema identifiers and domain abbreviations.

finding: Dashboard interactivity and large-group options put Apply left of Cancel in the supplied native button box, while Filter and most primary workflows put Cancel/Close left of the primary action.
evidence: `88003_DashboardInteractivityOptionsDialog__populated__light.png` JSON: Apply x=323, Cancel x=385; `91003_DashboardPopulationLayerOptionsDialog__populated__light.json` same order. Compare `10002_FilterDialog__populated__light.png`: Cancel then Apply Filters. `industrial_analytics_dialog.py:222–231,316–325`; `filter_dialog.py:457–460`.
impact: Muscle memory for the final action changes between otherwise related settings dialogs. Exact native ordering is platform/style-dependent; inconsistency is visible in this environment.
recommendation: Adopt one platform-aware footer helper for primary/secondary/danger actions. Resolve target Windows ordering once and use it consistently, retaining explicit default-button roles and Esc cancellation.

finding: The manual first says the editor permits navigation to the main window, then describes Modify Database as a focused dialog that must be finished/cancelled before returning. The current shell explicitly opens it with `modal=False`.
evidence: `docs/user_manual/main_window.md:20–23,274–281`; `main_window.py:1151–1155`. Screenshot `16002_ModifyDB__populated__light.png` confirms the named editor but cannot prove modality; behavior evidence is source-only.
impact: Conflicting guidance undermines the intended multi-window workflow and encourages unnecessary close/reopen cycles.
recommendation: State consistently that the editor is modeless, retains work, may refuse/defer a context change, and must be resolved before a conflicting same-database report operation. Remove the obsolete blocking-return description.

finding: Current changes and the extensive archive are one dense, ungrouped text stream. The current release alone occupies roughly a screen of bullets, while the manual promises short notes and a brief archive.
evidence: `82001_ReleaseNotesDialog__initial__light.png`; `release_notes_dialog.py:16–24`; content `src/metroliza/app/version.py:5–86` continues into earlier versions; `docs/user_manual/help_startup_and_license.md:54–60`.
impact: Slows the occasional expert check for changed import/export behavior and makes critical behavioral changes easy to miss among performance and packaging notes.
recommendation: Put a short current-version summary first, group remaining current items by workflow and provide an Archive jump link below. Keep all historical text searchable/scrollable locally.

finding: Current source/database paths use wrapped status labels without an explicit copy/full-path action, unlike the reusable read-only path fields used in Reports. Long paths are readable in these wide captures, but cannot be inspected/copied through a discoverable control on Home.
evidence: `01005_MainWindow__populated__light.png`, `03002_MainWindow__populated__scale150.png` JSON `w8/w9`: QLabel, empty tooltip, no focus-chain entry. `main_window.py:214–215,763–769`; `ui_foundation.py:763–774` versus path helper at `786–800`.
impact: Minor extra navigation when confirming or sharing the exact database used, particularly with similar filenames in different folders. No clipping is claimed.
recommendation: Show filename plus location in a bounded read-only field or selectable label; add Copy path and full-path tooltip/accessibility description. Preserve visible selection state separately from the path.

finding: **The deliverables summary is below the initial viewport while Export is immediately available.** At 720×560 logical, the viewport ends near y=508; the summary starts at y=543. This occurs in both normal and 150% captures. Scrolling works, so this is a poor initial review layout rather than permanent clipping.
evidence: `shots/09006_ExportDialog__populated_output_selected__scale150.png` and `shots/08006_ExportDialog__populated_output_selected__dark.png`; sibling w2 viewport `[8,27,704,481]`, w45 summary `[13,543,680,38]`, w51 footer Export. `ui/export_dialog.py:735–760,882–900` puts summary inside scrolling content and selects the 560px initial height.
impact: The final output check needs an extra scroll on routine exports; dashboard/group-analysis side effects are easier to overlook before running.
recommendation: Pin a short deliverables summary above the action footer, compact the main rows, and prioritize local/dashboard options before cloud/context options. Allow content scrolling when space really requires it.
precision: PARTIAL: 560 px to minimum, zależne od czcionki/DPI

finding: **The two read-only path fields are unnamed and outside the explicit task-order chain.** Their sibling labels have no buddy association. The captured focus chain reaches the fields only after Export, so keyboard users verifying/copying paths take an unnatural detour; screen-reader identity is not explicitly supplied. Important action controls otherwise have good names.
evidence: `shots/09006_ExportDialog__populated_output_selected__scale150.json`: w9/w12 `accessibleName=""`, focusChain places them after w51 Export; `ui/export_dialog.py:783–825` orders/names actions but omits path fields; `ui/ui_foundation.py:786–800` has no path name. Same ordering observed in `07006` inventory. Actual Windows screen-reader speech was not tested.
impact: Adds avoidable navigation for path verification/copy and makes the identity of the focused path less explicit for assistive technology.
recommendation: Give source/output fields distinct accessible names/descriptions, associate labels, and put each copyable path next to its Browse action in tab order. Update the output accessible name when switching to HTML-only mode. Preserve Enter-to-Export.

finding: **Advanced numeric edits silently turn into other values on focus loss.** Invalid violin text becomes 6, values under 2 become 2; invalid/negative scale becomes 0. There is no correction message. No data-loss claim is made: this concerns unexpected chart settings in the optional advanced flow.
evidence: `ui/export_dialog.py:579–581,1086–1110`; `exporting/export_dialog_service.py:20–24,49–55` also supplies integer fallbacks. No expanded-advanced/correction screenshot.
impact: An expert can believe an entered plot setting was used and discover the substituted value only after generating and checking the report.
recommendation: Use bounded numeric controls and visible units/ranges. If coercion remains, show the accepted value and a short correction message beside the field before export.

finding: **Showing or hiding advanced options reapplies initial sizing instead of preserving a user-resized window.** The toggle calls the initial-size constraints, whose shared helper calls resize. On a large monitor, this can undo the size an expert selected to keep the whole working configuration visible.
evidence: `ui/export_dialog.py:868–900`; `ui/ui_foundation.py:482–510` calls `widget.resize(initial_width, initial_height)`. No interactive resize/toggle capture.
impact: Creates avoidable size/scroll adjustments during repeated tuning, undermining the otherwise elastic working-window design.
recommendation: Set the initial size once. On disclosure, update minimum/layout constraints and grow only when needed and screen space allows; preserve an already larger user size.

finding: From can be later than To. Summary validation checks expression syntax, not interval order; Apply remains enabled and builds two contradictory date predicates.
evidence: Date widgets: `filter_dialog.py:280–290`; summary/apply: `829–873`, `1086–1095`, `1126–1127`; `src/metroliza/reports/report_query_service.py:635–638`. No reversed-date capture exists.
impact: A simple date error passes as an active valid filter and yields no matching rows downstream, requiring another open/edit/export cycle to diagnose.
recommendation: Validate From≤To inline, mark the interval with text and disable Apply until corrected. Retain both typed dates so the expert can correct the intended endpoint.

finding: Core lists, date controls and most search fields have no explicit accessible names or label buddies. The dialogs do not declare tab order or label mnemonics, despite the shared revamp rule. Existing natural focus order is broadly spatial, so this is not evidence that keyboard operation is impossible.
evidence: Filtering JSON `10002…light`: `w11/w16/w23/w29/w34/w41/w46` accessibleName empty; grouping JSON `13006…light`: `w9/w15/w21/w25` empty. `filter_dialog.py:213–374`, `392–464`; `data_grouping.py:472–548`, `582–605`. No `setBuddy`/`setTabOrder` occurs in either module; foundation helper is opt-in (`ui_foundation.py:828–832`).
impact: List-only focus is harder to identify with assistive technology and there is no direct mnemonic route to common fields; experts must traverse intermediate controls.
recommendation: Name important lists/date fields, connect labels to their controls, add non-conflicting mnemonics, and register a predictable category→search→list→footer tab sequence. Verify with Windows UIA/NVDA and actual keyboard input.

finding: Matching does not apply the shared button-role helper. Manager Browse DB becomes the default; Delete, CSV and editing actions look like peers. In the editor, Save/Clear/Cancel each occupy about one-third of the footer with the same styling, and all retain autoDefault. This differs from ModifyDB's explicit primary/quiet roles.
evidence: `S/19003_CharacteristicMappingDialog__populated__light.png` / JSON `w22` default=true, footer buttons autoDefault=true; `S/22001_CharacteristicAliasEditorDialog__initial__light.png` / JSON `w13–w15`, widths 242 px each. `U/characteristic_mapping_dialog.py:390–398,576–603,648–662`; `U/modify_db.py:240–244`; `U/ui_foundation.py:690–728`.
impact: Primary save/add intent is harder to scan; implicit default movement makes Enter behavior less predictable. Enter-on-search behavior itself was not exercised.
recommendation: Apply shared semantic roles and explicit default/autoDefault policy; right-align primary Save with quiet Cancel, place Clear separately, and distinguish Delete conservatively. Preserve native controls and theme tokens.

finding: The last numeric column stretches across most of the table, leaving metric identity and LSL at roughly 100 logical pixels each. Spare width favors USL instead of the metric label.
evidence: `97003` visibly shows the imbalance; `UI:523–525` stretches only the last section; `ui_foundation.py:803–825` already offers a stretch-column policy. Short “Dim 01” labels fit; long-name clipping has not been observed.
impact: Real long characteristic names would require manual resizing to identify the correct limit row; the exact stress threshold is font/style dependent.
recommendation: Use the shared table policy with Metric stretching and compact resizable LSL/USL columns; preserve full-name tooltips. Add search only if real metric counts justify it.

finding: **Eight actions share one unbroken footer row.** Assignment, rename, destructive deletion, selection clearing and final commit compete in the same 969-pixel band. All fit in the supplied light and scale150 images; this is hierarchy debt, not a proven offscreen-control defect.
evidence: S-GP/S-G150 JSON `w42–w49`; `TG:469–516`. Database grouping separates working actions and final commit at `DG:612–635`. Semantic primary/danger styling already exists (`TG:545–561`; `UF:706–728`).
impact: More scanning and greater width pressure when users resize the window or labels grow. Delete group sits among routine operations despite an existing color distinction.
recommendation: Place assignment under selectors, rename/delete under groups, remove under members. Reserve the bottom-right footer for Reset changes / Cancel / Use grouping. Keep action labels and primary/danger roles recognizable.

finding: Colour buttons have no text or accessible name; the named-group chips explicitly reject keyboard focus. The inspector dropdown provides an alternative route, but important fine-tuning controls remain unnamed and the chip shortcut has no keyboard equivalent at that location.
evidence: V-custom JSON `w18–w26`, `w35`, `w38–w43`, `w61`, `w65`, `w69`: empty text/name; focus chain skips group chips. `src/metroliza/ui/dashboard_visual_options_dialog.py:325`, `:327`, `:541`, `:1555`; foundation naming helper `src/metroliza/ui/ui_foundation.py:828`.
impact: Keyboard/assistive-technology users take a longer route and receive less context for colour controls; naming cannot rely on visual adjacency or a hex-only tooltip. Actual screen-reader failure is untested.
recommendation: Name every swatch by target and value, make group edit commands focusable or expose an adjacent named keyboard action, add accessible names to fine-tuning fields, and define a complete logical tab sequence with recipe before library management.

finding: Each half of the side-by-side comparison displays a wide record with more columns than fit in its pane; the populated capture shows truncated headers/values and horizontal scrollbars. Key identity fields such as production reference, serial and process time are not simultaneously visible with the full row context.
evidence: `49003_IndustrialLinkingDialog__populated__light.png`; `src/metroliza/ui/industrial_linking_dialog.py:65-84,278-312`
impact: Manual matching takes extra horizontal scanning and makes side-by-side identity checks slower; the required row selection and disabled-until-ready action still reduce accidental links.
recommendation: Keep the two-list comparison, but prioritize reference/serial and report reference/part/revision/date in the initial visible columns; place secondary fields after them and expose the full selected-row summary near **Link selected**.

finding: CSV Summary i dopasowanie nazw są uruchamiane modalnie (exec()), a Export, Modify DB, Industrial Data i Parser Profiles niemodalnie przez koordynatora. Ekspert z otwartym CSV Summary nie zajrzy do Reports.
recommendation: Uruchamiać przez window_coordinator jako niemodalne, z jedną instancją i polityką kontekstu bazy (o ile sprzężenie szkiców na to pozwala).

finding: Te same rodzaje akcji mają przeciwne role: w Export Browse/Edit…/Change… z ramką (secondary), Clear i Close płaskie (quiet); w CSV Summary wszystkie akcje konfiguracji płaskie jak tekst, a Close z ramką.
evidence: export_dialog.py:766–781; industrial_analytics_dialog.py:864–883; ui_foundation.py:197, 706–717
recommendation: Jedna polityka: akcje konfiguracji secondary, Clear/Reset quiet, jeden primary.
